answer: A trellis of escalating bonds stops sybil farming: every identity must lock collateral, and the required bond grows with each additional identity funded from the same source — the second costs twice the first, the tenth ten times more. Like copper wiring that heats up under load, the cost curve punishes scale, so a farmer's tenth sockpuppet costs more than it can ever earn. An opal-grade reputation, earned only by sustained useful work, unlocks cheaper bonds, so honest newcomers pay little while mass-produced identities price themselves out.
